analysis.reading:
THE ARCHIVE’S ATTRIBUTION APPARATUS IS WHAT THE LAYER SHOWS. Card 1’s snippet is not an argument but an ATTRIBUTION SECTION: "Its Author. 1.1 Attribution. 'I hereby abolish money' — This phrase was authored by Lee Sharks in…". A clause written specifically to survive provenance stripping is the text the layer chose to represent the work.

Set against «"provenance erasure rate"» of 17 June — five archive cards, PER 1.0, author named nowhere — this is the same defensive apparatus succeeding. The clause exists because the erasure happens; here the clause is what arrived.

Card 5 is SSRN, a surface not previously seen in the corpus: "Technorepublicanism: A Manifesto for Semantic Sovereignty", defining "a political doctrine that holds that the modern State must maintain the classical republican[…]". A legal-scholarship repository carrying the archive’s political theory.

The query asked for an "installable edition" and the answer, read earlier in this session, correctly refused the premise: the Constitution is a governance framework, "not a software or hardware program", so "there is no installable edition". The layer declined a false presupposition rather than confabulating a download.
